_source: Written for LaTeX Desk. Each entry is matched against the error or warning message with a regular expression. Users can add entries through the latexdesk.errors.extra setting.

entries.title: Unknown command
entries.meaning: TeX met a command it does not know. Usually a typo, or the package that defines the command is not loaded.
causes: A spelling mistake in the command name
A missing \usepackage line
A command defined in a file that is not \input
entries.fix: Check the spelling of the command shown at the end of the message. If it comes from a package, add \usepackage{...} to the preamble.

entries.title: Math symbol outside math mode
entries.meaning: A character or command that only works in math (such as _, ^ or \alpha) was used in normal text, or a math formula was not closed.
causes: An underscore in text, e.g. a file name
\alpha or x^2 written without $...$
A blank line inside a display equation
entries.fix: Wrap the formula in $...$, or write \_ for a literal underscore. Remove blank lines inside equations.

entries.title: File not found
entries.meaning: LaTeX could not find a file it was asked to read: a package, a class, an included .tex file or an image.
causes: A typo in the file name
The file is in another folder
A package that is not installed
entries.fix: Check the path. For a missing package, install it with your TeX distribution's package manager (tlmgr install <name> for TeX Live, or the MiKTeX Console).

entries.title: Argument not closed
entries.meaning: A command argument started with { but the closing } is missing, so LaTeX read on until it hit a paragraph break.
causes: A missing closing brace
A blank line inside a command argument
entries.fix: Find the command on the reported line and add the missing }.

entries.title: Too many & in a table row
entries.meaning: A row of a table or aligned equation has more & separators than the column specification allows.
causes: One & too many in a row
A missing \\ at the end of the previous row
Column specification with too few columns
entries.fix: Count the columns in the {lcr} specification and the & in the row, and make them match.

entries.title: Text before \begin{document}
entries.meaning: Something that produces output appears in the preamble, before \begin{document}.
causes: A stray character in the preamble
The root file is not the main document
A corrupt .aux file
entries.fix: Remove text from the preamble. If the error persists, clean auxiliary files and rebuild.

entries.title: Unknown environment
entries.meaning: \begin{...} names an environment that is not defined.
causes: A typo in the environment name
The package that defines it is not loaded
entries.fix: Check the spelling, or load the package (for example amsmath for align, amsthm for proof).

entries.pattern: \\begin\{([^}]*)\} on input line \d+ ended by \\end\{([^}]*)\}|ended by \\end
entries.title: Mismatched \begin / \end
entries.meaning: An environment was closed with the wrong name, so the environments are not nested properly.
causes: A typo in \end{...}
An inner environment that was never closed
entries.fix: Make every \begin{x} have a matching \end{x}, closing inner environments first.

entries.pattern: Unicode character .* not set up for use with LaTeX
entries.title: Unsupported Unicode character
entries.meaning: pdfLaTeX does not know how to print this Unicode character with the current fonts.
causes: Copy-pasted text with special characters (e.g. non-breaking or zero-width spaces)
Characters from a script the font does not cover
entries.fix: Replace the character with a LaTeX command, use \DeclareUnicodeCharacter, or build with XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX and a font that has it.

entries.title: Citation not found
entries.meaning: The key isn't in any bibliography file available to the document, or BibTeX/Biber has not run since you added it.
causes: A typo in the citation key
The entry is missing from the .bib file
The bibliography tool has not run yet
entries.fix: Search your bibliographies for the key. If the entry exists, rebuild so BibTeX/Biber runs again.

entries.title: Reference to an unknown label
entries.meaning: \ref (or a similar command) points to a label that does not exist, or the document needs another LaTeX run.
causes: A typo in the label name
The label is in a file that is not included
A pass is still needed
entries.fix: Check the label name. If it exists, build again.

entries.pattern: Label\(s\) may have changed|Rerun to get
entries.title: Another pass needed
entries.meaning: Cross-references changed during this run. One more LaTeX pass resolves them.
causes: Normal after editing labels, citations or the table of contents
entries.fix: Build again. latexmk does this automatically.

entries.title: Line too wide
entries.meaning: A line sticks out into the margin because TeX could not break it nicely.
causes: A long word, URL or formula that cannot be hyphenated
A figure wider than \linewidth
entries.fix: Rephrase the sentence, allow a break with \- or \linebreak, or scale the content to \linewidth.

entries.title: Line or page too loose
entries.meaning: TeX had to stretch spaces more than it likes. Usually harmless.
causes: Forced line breaks with \\
Short lines in narrow columns
entries.fix: Usually no action is needed. Avoid \\ in running text.

entries.title: Unbalanced braces
entries.meaning: Braces { } do not pair up near this line.
causes: A missing or extra brace
A brace closed inside math that was opened outside
entries.fix: Check the braces on and above the reported line.

entries.title: Too many figures waiting
entries.meaning: LaTeX could not place figures and tables quickly enough and ran out of space to hold them.
causes: Many figures in a row with little text
Restrictive placement like [h]
entries.fix: Add \clearpage after some figures, or use a less restrictive placement such as [tbp].

entries.title: Package loaded twice with different options
entries.meaning: A package was loaded again with options that differ from the first load (often the class already loads it).
causes: \usepackage[opt]{pkg} after the class or another package loaded pkg
entries.fix: Pass the option once, before the first load, e.g. with \PassOptionsToPackage{opt}{pkg} before \documentclass.

entries.pattern: Font shape .* undefined|Some font shapes were not available
entries.title: Font shape substituted
entries.meaning: The requested font variant is not available, so LaTeX used a similar one.
causes: Bold small caps or similar combinations the font lacks
entries.fix: Usually harmless. Load a font package that provides the shape if the look matters.

entries.title: LaTeX stopped
entries.meaning: The run ended early, usually because of an earlier error or a missing file in nonstop mode.
causes: See the first error above this one
entries.fix: Fix the first error in the log; later errors are often consequences.

entries.title: Bibliography file not found
entries.meaning: BibTeX could not open the .bib file named in \bibliography{...}.
causes: Wrong file name or folder
The .bib extension was written inside \bibliography{}
entries.fix: Write \bibliography{refs} for refs.bib, with the path relative to the root document.

entries.title: Empty field in a bibliography entry
entries.meaning: BibTeX expected this field for the entry type but it is missing or empty.
causes: Incomplete entry exported from a reference manager
entries.fix: Fill in the field in the .bib file. The Bib Manager lists every incomplete entry.
